question: If a fake porn of a girl has been shown and circulated to defame her then what could be the punushment for the person who tried to defame that girl?( Hooghly, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,If someone creates or circulates a fake pornographic video of a girl to defame her, it is a serious criminal offense in India under multiple sections of the law.Such an act is punishable under various sections of the Information Technology Act, 2000, and the Indian Penal Code. Under Section 67 and 67A of the IT Act, transmitting obscene or sexually explicit content electronically can lead to imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to Rs. 10 lakhs. Additionally, under IPC Sections 469 and 500 for defamation and forgery to harm reputation, the offender can be punished with imprisonment up to three years. Section 509 IPC, which deals with insulting the modesty of a woman, can also apply and carries a sentence of up to three years. If the content is morphed or AI-generated (deepfake), it still qualifies as cybercrime and forgery, and the accused can be prosecuted accordingly. These laws are designed to protect individuals from digital harassment and uphold their dignity and privacy.

question: whether defamation case can be filed both under civil and criminal law( Chennai, Tamil Nadu )
answer: Dear Client,A person aggrieved by defamation has a right to proceed both in the civil Court as well as in the criminal Court. He can take either one or the other or both courses. Law does not debar him from enforcing civil and criminal rights at the same time. In India, defamation is categorized as either criminal or civil, and both types are covered by the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC). In Civil Defamation, a person who is defamed can move the competent Court having pecuniary jurisdiction and seek damages in the form of monetary compensation. Under Section 19 of the Civil Procedure Code (CPC), a civil suit can be filed either where the Defendant resides or where the Defamatory statement was made/published. A defamation of a criminal nature has been codified under Sections 499 and 500 of the Indian Penal Code 1860 and to file a criminal suit under this Section, a person must have made an imputation about another person with either an intention, knowledge, or reason to believe that such an imputation will harm the reputation of the said person. Under criminal defamation, individuals can be charged with an offense punishable by imprisonment for two years or a fine. As per the Limitation Act, there is a limitation period of one year for filing a civil defamation suit and the limitation to file a criminal defamation complaint is 3 years from the period of knowledge of offense.

answer: Dear Client,In the hit-and-run case, police filed an FIR on both the persons involved in a road accident under Sec. 279 of IPC(now Section 281 of BNS) for rash and negligent driving and Section 337 of IPC (now Section 125 of BNS)  for causing hurt to any person. Both offenses are cognizable and bailable offence and triable by a Magistrate. On appeal, bail can be provided by the police officer who has custody of the offender or by the court. To obtain bail, a bail bond needs to be executed, with or without the presence of sureties.   In motor accident cases both the owner and driver of the vehicle are liable to face prosecution proceedings initiated before the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal once an FIR is lodged in the police station in hit and run case and the legal heirs of the deceased victim and the injured persons apply to the Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 within six months of the occurrence of the accident.  Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019) states that the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay compensation of five lakh rupees in case of death or two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be. The claimant is not required to prove that the death or grievous hurt was due to any wrongful act or neglect of the owner or any other person. In this context, the judgment passed by the Calcutta High Court in the case of Senjuti Roy (Nee Sengupta) VS New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and the judgment passed by the Rajasthan High Court in the case of Ganesh Bairwa VS Ramphool Bairwa may be referred. Given the complexity of the motor accident case as stated in the query that involves delayed registration of the vehicle, driving a vehicle on the road without insurance and other vital documents, absconding of a vehicle in hit and run case, contradictory statements of the witnesses and finally the investigation report of the police, the Tribunal may pass an order for payment of compensation to the claimant against the defaulted parties. Fine as a penalty is imposed only if there is a criminal prosecution. You have to establish the fact before the Court denying that you were not driving the vehicle rashly and that the accident arose not on account of your negligence. You have to take the defense that in spite of cautious driving you met with an accident. Unless you plead guilty generally fine is not imposed. The maximum fine for both offences is around Rs.1500. under Section 279 and 337 IPC if you are ready to plead guilty then the court will impose the fine and close the case but it is better if you can engage the service of an Advocate to navigate the issue in the right way. You may like to contest the case but the court case will drag you for years and you may have to waste your time, energy, and money on litigation as well as lawyer fees which may be ten times the amount that you may pay as a fine, hence better pay the fine amount, which appears to be very minimum and come out of this crisis.

question:
I strongly contested the anticipatory bail of the accused, however, court has granted the AB to the accused. This accused's application for AB was u/s 438 of Cr.P.C.

After 2 days of granting AB, accused applied for relaxation/modification of conditions and within 12 days, final order was given and conditions were relaxed. However, I was not aware of this relaxation/modification since I was not party respondent but only the State/Police.

Shouldn't Judge be asking for my/complainant's SAY during relaxation application under 439(1)(b) since initially I already opposed/contested accused's anticipatory bail under 438 of Cr.P.C? Is there any Supreme Court case law supporting the same that says complainant should be given the chance to be heard before modifying the conditions as the conditions involve complainant that he should be threatened, induced, contacted etc?( Mumbai, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Yes, the judge should have given you an opportunity to be heard before modifying the conditions of the accused's anticipatory bail under Section 439(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC). This is because you are the complainant in the case and the conditions of the anticipatory bail directly affect your safety and security. Under Section 439(1)(b) of the Criminal Procedure Code, the court has the power to modify or revoke any conditions of bail at any time during the bail period. However, the court must give notice to the public prosecutor or the complainant of the hearing of the application for modification of bail conditions and hear their objections.The Supreme Court of India has held in several cases that the complainant should be given a chance to be heard before modifying the conditions of anticipatory bail. In the case of Lalita Kumari v. State of Uttar Pradesh, the Supreme Court held that "the complainant has a right to be heard when the question of modification of conditions imposed on the grant of anticipatory bail arises." In another case, Shashi Kant Jha v. State of Bihar, the Supreme Court held that "the complainant should be given an opportunity to be heard before the conditions of anticipatory bail are modified, as the complainant is the person who is most affected by the modification of the conditions."Therefore, you should file an application with the court to set aside the order modifying the conditions of the anticipatory bail. In your application, you should argue that you were not given an opportunity to be heard before the modification of the conditions.

question: I have taken personal loan and 2 credit cards, as my father got severe burnt due to this my financial situation become weak and now unable to pay. Today I got notice from the bank under sector 25 of pssa 2007( Faridabad, Haryana )
answer: Dear Client,Section 25 of the Payment and Settlement System Act 2007(PSSA), states that if an electronic transfer cannot be completed due to insufficient money or if an amount required to be paid out exceeds the limit on the credit card of the payer, the payer can be imprisoned or fined twice the amount or both similar to the dishonor of a cheque under the Negotiable Instruments Act 1881. Section 25 of the Act states that the payee, before filing a complaint under said Act to recover money, must inform the payer via a written notification/legal notice seeking payment of the dishonored amount. If the person initiating an electronic funds transfer does not pay the money to the beneficiary within 15 days of receiving the legal notice, a complaint is filed before the Court for recovery of dues/loan. So, on receipt of notice under Sec.25 of PSSA, you should try your best to negotiate the loan with the lender/financier. You can try to negotiate a debt settlement on your own (under OTS- One-time settlement scheme) if your pocket permits, but sometimes it's typically done through third parties like debt relief companies, which you may hire to negotiate the settlement matter with the lender on your behalf. With this method, you will make payments to the debt settlement company rather than your creditors/lenders, along with the payment of fees or service charges. Debt settlement is an agreement between a lender Bank and a borrower in which the borrower repays a portion of a loan balance and the lender forgives the balance. You may consider starting the negotiation by offering to pay 25% or 30% of your outstanding balance in return for forgiveness on the rest. But, it may be noted that while there are legitimate debt relief/settlement companies, there are also many fraud/scam operations. So, if you're considering one, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau(CFPB) suggests contacting your state Attorney General's(AG) office and local consumer protection agency to ask if they have any consumer complaints pending on file about that company. Some states require that debt settlement companies be licensed, which may provide some added protection. Although a debt settlement can offload some of your financial burden, there are also a few potential risks and downsides to consider. First, a debt settlement will affect your credit score in CIBIL. That will make it more difficult for you to get credit or good interest rates in the future. Another potential drawback is that when you settle debt, you could face tax consequences. Finally, when you settle a debt with a credit card company, your account is closed once the settlement is complete. So you could potentially have no credit facility to use a credit card further owing to your poor credit score. Further, a quick counseling session with a certified credit counselor can help you discover your options and choose the right path forward.

question: How many times and in front of whom does the woman victim have to give her statement and appearance after FIR for molestation has been lodged? answer: Dear Client,In this context, Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Investigation and Prosecution of victims of rape/sexual assault circulated by the Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt of India may be referred wherein it is stated that  1) The victim of such crime should be treated with honor and sensitivity.  The officer interacting with her (the victim) should be extremely courteous. No indecent questions should be put to the victim. Care should be taken to protect dignity and prevent embarrassing situations for the victim. The identity of the victim should not be made public and due care should be taken not to reveal her identity in print and electronic media. 2) A copy of the FIR shall be sent immediately within 24 hours to the Magistrate under Section 157, Cr.P.C. 3) Investigation of crime against women shall be conducted by a woman officer. There should be, at least, one lady officer on the investigating team. 4) As regards the recording of the statement of the victim under section 161, Cr.P.C, the victim should not be called to the police station. The statement of the victim should be recorded at the residence of the victim or in the place of her choice by a woman police officer in the presence of parents or guardians or a near relative or a social worker of the locality. 5) It shall be the duty of the investigating officer/SHO to inform the Judicial Magistrate for the recording of the statement of the person against whom such an offence has been committed, as soon as the commission of offence is brought to the notice of the police (as mandated under sub-section (5-A) of Section 164, Cr.P.C. A copy of the statement under Section 164, Cr.P.C. should be handed over to the investigating officer immediately with specific directions that the content of such statement under Section 164, Cr.P.C. should not be disclosed to any person till the charge sheet/report under Section 173, Cr.P.C. is filed. A copy of the report of the medical examination of the victim, if any, should be immediately handed over to the Magistrate who records Promptly the statement of the victim under section 164, Cr.P.C. In cases of a delay exceeding 24 hours in taking the victim to the Magistrate, the Investigating officer should record the reasons for the same in the case diary and hand over a copy of the same to the Magistrate. 6) Section 164(A),Cr.P.C. imposes an obligation on the part ofinvestigating officer to get the victim of rape medically examined within 24 hours from the time of receiving the information relating to the commission of such offense. The report of such medical examination should be immediately forwarded to the Magistrate by the I.O., who records the statement of the victim under section 164, Cr.P.C. The victim as well as the accused person should be sent for medical examination by the I.O. under a properly filled-in, medicalexamination sheet. The female victim shall be examined medically, only by a lady doctor or under her supervision. A Rape victim above 18 years of age can be examined only after obtaining her written consent. A copy of the report of such examination shall be furnished by the medical officer, or registered medical practitioner, as the case may be, to the victim or her parents/guardian. All offences against women shall be promptly investigated and charge sheets should be filed in the court of law within sixty days as per section 173 Cr.P.C. While briefing media about sex crimes, the identity of the victim should not be disclosed. Under no circumstances, should the victim be produced before the media. Authorized officers alone, should brief the media. Therefore, given the protocol or SPPs of the MHA, if any unethical issues are observed in the investigation by the police, you can file a complaint with the Chairperson, State Human Rights Commission or the State Police Complaint Authority, which are independent bodies empowered to investigate any complaints against police officials. Section 191 of the said Act states that any person who is legally bound by an oath or affirmation to state the truth of any matter and makes a false statement in his/her affidavit is guilty of the offense of perjury which carries with it the possibility of imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine. Further, Section 193 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 states that any person who makes a false statement in an affidavit or any other document, knowing it to be false, shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. Section 191 of the IPC deals with the filing of false evidence, while section 340 of the Cr. PC outlines the process for making a complaint for this offense. Perjury is defined as the filing of false evidence or a false affidavit before a court knowing that it is false.

Impleading a person as a necessary party is a person who ought to have joined as a party and in whose absence no effective decree could be passed at all by the court. If a necessary party is not impleaded, the suit itself is liable to be dismissed. Since it is difficult to have an eyewitness to prove an illicit relationship; it can be proved indirectly by showing evidence such as hotel bills or travel records. question: In my case Prosecution sanction has issued demanding money for recording Measurements Book, that was not my duty, while ACB challan has framed charges for demanding money for signing completion certificate. When and at what stage I should challenge it. How I can get benifits for this .( Jaipur, Rajasthan )
answer: Dear Client,Under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, sanction for prosecution is required for an offence punishable under Sections 7, 10, 11, 13, 15 of the Act, while under Section 197(1) Cr. P.C. sanction is required for an offence committed by a public servant while acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty, and not otherwise. After the amendment of the Prevention of Corruption Act, in 2018, it significantly extended the provisions of PCA and gave it the required edge to tackle bribery/corruption involving commercial entities/private companies. According to Section 9 of the amended Act, a commercial organization can be held liable âif any person associated with such commercial organization gives or promises to give any undue advantage to a public servantâ with an intent to obtain or retain business or any advantage for that commercial organization. This provision covers all types of entities (including domestic companies, foreign companies, and partnerships) doing business in India. Thus, while the PCA, 1988 applied to public sector employees, the Act has been amended to encompass situations where private organizations and individuals can also be held accountable for indulging in corrupt practices. Further, the CBI investigates cases of corruption in compliance with the provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988, under the supervision of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC). This can include cases of bribery, extortion, and other forms of corruption. The CBI has a special division called the Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB). This branch handles the investigation of corruption-related cases. The CBI can initiate suo moto investigations on the basis of information received from the public, the media, or other sources. CBI lays great emphasis on catching corrupt public servants who demand and take bribes. The process of catching such corrupt public servants red-handed while they demand and take bribes is popularly called the 'trap'. It is not a legal term. A set procedure has been devised in CBI to lay a trap against a corrupt public servant. The evidence collected during the process of trap is placed before the court along with the charge sheet and is quite important in securing the conviction of the public servant charged with corruption. So, given the proposition of relevant laws, you may choose the recourse/steps that suit your grievance most in the prevailing situation, If required, hire an experienced Advocate to navigate the issues in the right way.

It is essential to prove to the court that the FIR was lodged with malicious intent to cause harm or inconvenience and is devoid of truth. The burden of proof rests on the petitioner. The accused is charged u/s 366 IPC and pleaded not guilty of the charges and the summons were served upon PWs. the victim in her statement u/s164 stated that she had love and affairs with accused person and they solemnised their marriage and she lived with accused for one month thereafter she appeared before the I.O of the case she was taken to hospital but she refused her medical examination. When the victim girl appeared before the court she in her examination in chief stated that accused forcibly took her and taken her to a unknown place and she stayed there for one phone. Prosecution exhibited her original birth certificate which reveals her age was 17 years at the time of occurrence. The statement of victim u/s 164 was also exhibited. 
The informant in her examination in chief stated that she didn't see any occurrence and other witnesses were also gave hearsay evidence and there is absence of Corroborative evidence supporting the version of victim. But it is a fact that  victim was a minor at the time of occurrence, the defense in cross examination only gave suggestion that at the time of occurrence she was above 18 years, but her evidence is marked by flaws and gaps in such a situation whether it is proved that the victim was minor at the time of occurrence or prosecution succeed in proving the essential condition of section 366 IPC. and whether the prosecution will suceeds in securing a conviction of accused. please help with suggestion in preparing the argument of this case with landmark judgement in the light of the present case.( Cachar, Assam )
answer: Dear Client,The essential condition for the application of Section 366 I.P.C. is that there is kidnapping or abduction of a woman with the intention to compel her or knowing it to be likely that she will be compelled to marry any person against her will or will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse. Section 366 I.P.C. only applies when the woman abducted has no intention of marriage or lawful intercourse when abducted. Mere abduction does not bring the accused under the ambit of this penal section. In Shahjahan Vs. State, 2011 Cr.L.J. 573, the Supreme Court has held that to establish an offence u/s 366 I.P.C., it must first be established that the offence of kidnapping under Section 361 I.P.C. or abduction under Section 362 I.P.C. has been proved. It must then be shown that such kidnapping or abduction was with the contumacious intent referred to under Section 366 I.P.C. Further, in the case of  Gabbu Vs. The state of M.P., AIR 2006 SC 2461, the Apex Court has held that so far as the charge u/s 366 I.P.C. is concerned, mere finding that a woman was abducted is not enough. It must further be proved that the abduction is for the purposes mentioned in Section 366 I.P.C. Given the provision of relevant law and averments of the Apex Court, you can defend your case to before the Court.

question: i had invested some money with a person who promised profits. After failing to return the money on time the person gave me post dated cheques that bounced. Post giving the cheques the person absconded. I have filed a cheque bounce case in 2022 but it has still not resolved. My question is how much time does it take for the bounce case to reach judgement. Also, since the accused is absconding will the case every reach judgement? Will there be money recovery in the case and what are the remedies for when the accused is absconding?( Mumbai, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Regarding your situation, filing a cheque bounce case under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, is the appropriate step. However, such cases can take time to resolve, typically ranging from a few months to several years, depending on the court's workload and the complexity of the case. Since the accused is absconding, the court can issue a non-bailable warrant (NBW) to secure his presence. If the accused remains untraceable, the court can declare him a proclaimed offender under Section 82 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC). This can further complicate and prolong the proceedings. While money recovery directly through this case may be challenging, you can also file a civil suit for recovery of the amount due. This dual approach might increase your chances of recovery. It is advisable to consult with your legal counsel to explore the possibility of attaching the absconder's properties as a means of securing the owed amount.

Once such a decree is passed, the defendant is permanently prohibited from the assertion of a right or from the commission of an act that would be contrary to the rights of the plaintiff. The grant of an injunction is subject to the provisions of Order 39, Section 94 (c) and (e) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 & Section 37(2) of the Specific Relief Act 1963. This examination is conducted under oath, and the substance of the examination is documented and signed by the complainant, witnesses, and the magistrate. If the magistrate finds sufficient grounds for proceeding with the case, he may issue a summons or warrant to the accused under Section 227 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). question:
I'm experiencing severe difficulty in helping my uncle to get his earnings and property papers. I have three brothers, and I am the youngest of all. My uncle, who is 69 years old, was never married and has no kids. He was a farmer and worked for my father his entire life. He worked selflessly for us and never demanded anything from my father and mother. My father, mother, and uncle lived together in a village in Bihar till my mother died in January 2023.Â 
My father and uncle inherited huge land property from their father (my grandfather). My father also has a home in Ranchi where my 1st elder brother has lived with his family for 27 years. After my mother's death, my father relocated to Ranchi with my uncle. But my sister-in-law (my 1st elder brother's wife) never liked my uncle and didn't take care of him at all. My uncle had cataracts, blood sugar, and high blood pressure, but he was never taken to a doctor for his treatment. Not only that, he was offered leftover food only two times a dayâ11 AM and 10 PM. She used to curse him for no reason.Â 
My uncle has only one eye, so I used to pressurize my 1st elder brother to get his cataract operation done. But he never did that. Because they (my brother and his wife) wanted my uncle to die soon. Finally, I brought him to Bangalore and got his cataract operation done after reducing his sugar level and blood pressure. In between, my father handed over all the property papers and bank account details of my uncle to my 1st brother. Now, my uncle is asking for his money and land papers from him, but he is not ready to give anything. I want to give my uncle his legal right, but I don't know where to start from.Â 

Any suggestion would be highly appreciated.( Bangalore, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,An individual gets the right to ancestral property by birth. Typically, ancestral property refers to property that has been inherited for four or more generations and has not been divided or sold off. If the title of the property was inherited by your father and uncle from your grandfather or great-grandfather, then the said property may be considered ancestral property. Until and unless an undivided ancestral property is partitioned through a decree of partition passed by a Civil Court, a coparcener or legal heir cannot get his/her share in the said property. In the given scenario, your uncle needs to file a civil suit for a declaration under Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 before the competent Civil Court seeking an order of injunction under Order 39, Rule 1 & 2 read with Section 151 of CPC praying the Court to exercise its inherent power to do justice. Apart from this, being a coparcener and legal heir of the said undivided ancestral property, your uncle can file a civil suit for partition before the competent civil court to obtain his share in the property.

For Section 498A, it is often filed by the woman or her family members, while Section 506 can be filed by anyone who has been threatened. Once a complaint is filed, the police may conduct an investigation, which could involve questioning the accused, witnesses, and the victim. In some cases, the accused may be arrested immediately, or the matter may proceed to court for a trial. The accused has the right to seek bail. question: How to apply for initiation of Perjury Crpc 340  proceedings against wife in Family court against her CrPC 125(3) application for Recovery, where she had applied for recovery money of our child , who is with me, she left at my home. what to do?( Jalgaon, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Giving false evidence in court is a criminal offense and an act of perjury. There are two pre-conditions for initiating proceedings under Section 340 CrPC: Firstly, the material produced before the Court must establish a prima facie case for a complaint for inquiry into an offense referred to in clause (b)(i) of sub-section (1) of Section 195 CrPC, and Secondly, it is expedient in the interests of justice that an inquiry should be made into the alleged offense.  Section 191 of the Indian Penal Code clearly says that who has given false evidence on oath is punishable under section 191 of the IPC.  In order to establish before the court that he/she has given false evidence you have to produce proof in family court and also file a complaint in Magistrate court that the party is giving false evidence on oath. In the application, you may ask for dismissal of his/her case because of perjury.  You may also ask the court to decide on the perjury application filed under Sce.340 Cr.PC first before disposing of the interim petition filed by him/her. if you are sure that the petitioner has submitted false facts and forged documents then you can submit an application under Section 191 of IPC in the Family Court where the application filed u/s.125(3) of Cr.PC is pending now and on receiving the application the court shall send the complaint to the Magistrate Court under Section 195 of CrPC and the receiving court shall initiate the proceedings of perjury under Section 340 of CrPC. The Apex Court in the case of Afzal & Anr. V. State Of Haryana, 1996, held that a false and misleading statement deliberately and wilfully made by a party to the proceedings to obtain a favorable order, amounts to prejudice or interference with the due course of judicial proceedings, and it will amount to criminal contempt.

question: an assistant engineer who works in governmemt company tsnpdcl who molested took advantage physically except intercourse but have attempted intercourse failed by giving hopes of marriage is denying to marry now then what are the laws applied on him and whether he can be terminated from his government job( Ramagundam, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,An aggrieved woman can file multiple cases against a person who cheated her with false promises of marriage if she can prove those allegations in Court. Section 90(now Section 28 of BNS) and Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code(now Section 63 of BNS) are what the person is charged with when he has a sexual relationship with a woman on false promise of marriage. Section 375 of IPC defines Rape and Section 90 IPC talks about consent when obtained using fear or misinformation. Section 114A of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 talks about the presumption as to the absence of consent in certain prosecutions for rape. This section states that if the woman testifies in a court of law that she had given consent under a false pretext of marriage, then it will be considered as consent given under a false promise of marriage. Consent given by a victim based on a false assumption would be a violation of Section 375 IPC and Section 90 IPC, respectively. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has declared that if a person's objective is to do evil and he has ulterior motivations, he will be guilty under section 376 IPC(now Section 64 of BNS) and if motive is not taken into consideration then more people with evil intent will exploit girls from the lowest and poorest section of society by luring them with false promises of marriage and forcing them to have physical relations while convincing them that they will marry in the future, thinking that law is on their side as they have obtained the consent. So, given the proposition of relevant laws and the averments of the Apex Court, you need to consult an Advocate experienced in criminal cases to navigate the issues in the right way. PC is not maintainable. An order that does not determine the rights of the parties but only one aspect of the suit or the trial is an interlocutory order. However, in the case of Amarnath and Ors. Vs. State of  Haryana and Anr., (1977) 4 SCC 137 the Hon'ble Supreme Court has defined interlocutory order stating that interlocutory orders must be those which decide the rights and liabilities of the parties which are purely interim or temporary in nature and do not decide or touch the important rights or liabilities of the parties. .Any order that substantially affects the rights of the accused, or decides certain rights of the parties cannot be said to be an interlocutory order so as to bar a revision to the High Court against that order, because that would be against the very object which formed the basis for insertion of this particular provision in Section 397 of the 1973 Code. Thus, orders which are matters of moment and which affect or adjudicate the rights of the accused on a particular aspect of the trial cannot be said to be interlocutory so as to be outside the purview of the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court.

answer: Dear Client,In legal matters, the choice between filing a writ of "Mandamus" or "Certiorari" depends on the specific circumstances of your case and the relief you are seeking. Both writs have different purposes and are used in distinct situations.1. **Writ of Mandamus:**- This writ is issued by a higher court to a lower court, tribunal, or public authority to perform a specific duty that it is legally obligated to do but has failed to fulfill.- It is generally not used for quashing proceedings but rather to compel an authority to act according to law.2. **Writ of Certiorari:**- This writ is used to quash the orders, decisions, or proceedings of inferior courts, tribunals, or authorities that are found to be without jurisdiction or contrary to the law.- It is commonly employed for quashing FIRs, chargesheets, or other legal processes.If you want to quash both the FIR and the chargesheet, and your argument revolves around the lack of jurisdiction or violation of legal principles, the writ of "Certiorari" would be more appropriate. This writ is commonly used to seek judicial review and quash proceedings that are deemed illegal or against the principles of natural justice.In your 482 application before the High Court, you can specifically request the court to issue a writ of "Certiorari" to quash both the FIR and the chargesheet if you believe there are legal grounds for doing so. Ensure that your application clearly outlines the legal points supporting the quashing and provides relevant facts and evidence.It is advisable to consult with a legal professional who can assess the specifics of your case and guide you on the most appropriate course of action based on the legal principles applicable in your jurisdiction.

answer: Dear Client,A writ of mandamus is typically issued by the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India when a public authority has failed or refused to perform a mandatory duty despite being requested to do so. A writ of mandamus compels a public authority to perform its legal duty, and the police are considered a public authority. You can mention police officials or government officials as the sole respondents in a mandamus writ petition if they are responsible for the alleged failure to perform a public duty. The writ of mandamus is primarily used against public authorities to compel them to perform their statutory duties. The names of the main accused can be included as respondents in a writ of mandamus petition, but only if they are also a public authority or have a public duty that is being violated. When a writ petition is heard on the merits, the court considers the substance of the claim, the evidence presented, and the legal arguments to decide whether the petitioner is entitled to the relief sought. The contents of the writ petition shall include: a clear statement of the facts, supporting documents, the specific relief sought, and a duly sworn affidavit verifying the facts. So, you can mention the inaction of the police on your complaint or private complaint in the writ petition. The advocate's fee for filing a writ of mandamus in the High Court can vary based on several factors, including the advocate's experience, the complexity of the case, costs associated with court fees and other expenses, and the specific High Court involved. question: Can sec 67A IT Act be compounded If the judge allows?( Mumbai, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Section 67A of the IT Act deals with the transmission or publication of sexually explicit content in electronic form and the offences under Section 67A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 are not usually compoundable. The punishment for an offence under Section 67A of the IT Act includes imprisonment and a fine. However, the High Court can make the offence compoundable by exercising its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 based on the facts and circumstances of the case. This issue has been decided by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case titled Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and Another (2012) 2 SCC (L&S) 998 wherein it was held that the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences Under Section 320 of the Code. Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation, but it has to be exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in such power to secure the ends of justice and/or to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

question: In what case scenario court gives brainmapping test without taking any concent of victim or accused?( Howrah, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,A court, including a district court, cannot compel an accused person to undergo a brain-mapping test, as this violates the fundamental right against self-incrimination under Article 20(3) of the Indian Constitution. However, the test can be administered if the accused voluntarily consents to the same. In the landmark case of Selvi v. State of Karnataka (2010), the Supreme Court ruled that no lie detector tests, including polygraph, narco-analysis, and brain-mapping tests, should be administered without the consent of the accused. Article 20(3) of the Constitution states that no person accused of an offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself and any such test can only be conducted with the express and voluntary consent of the accused to be recorded before a Judicial Magistrate. The Apex Court also ruled that the results of these tests cannot be admitted as direct evidence in court without the consent of the person undergoing the test. So, even if the victim appeals for it, in the absence of voluntary consent of the accused, the Court cannot pass an order for a brain-mapping test of the accused.

I have gone through the decision of Honâble Supreme court in the case of Vijay Madanlal Choudhary V/S Union of India in Special Leave Petition (Criminal) No 4634 of 2014 and also other judgements on PMLA. After reading the abovesaid decision and few articles by renowned lawyers on the said decision, my observations (some are copies from articles) are as under:
â¢	â¢ The Supreme Court upheld the validity of the powers under Sections 5, 8(4), 15, 17, 19, affirming that these provisions have a reasonable link to combating money laundering.
â¢	FIR is not required for investigation, though it is not mentioned in the judgement. This is affirmed by Honâble Delhi High Court in the case of Vir Bhadra Singh V/S Enforcement Directorate 2017 (3) RCR(Criminal) 576
â¢	The Courtâs endorsement of the reverse burden of proof places more responsibility on the accused in money laundering cases, which may make it harder for accused individuals to defend themselves unless they provide credible evidence of their innocence.
â¢	In  P. Chidambaram Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, (2019) 9 SCC 24, the Supreme Court has held that a âscheduled offenceâ is a sine qua non for the offence of money laundering which would generate the money that is being laundered. However, this judgment, nowhere states that the registration of FIR is a sine qua non. 
In view of my above observations, FIR is not a pre-condition for lodging a complaint with office of the Directorate of Enforcement. Alternatively Section 17 empowers Directorate of Enforcement is empowered to order for search and seizure of property. I sincerely request your team to provide me your opinion on my observations made as above.( Raigad, Maharashtra )

Union of India  (SLP (Criminal) No. 4634 of 2014) and other related judgments on the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA).Your observation is very much  correct. The Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of these provisions and affirmed that the powers conferred under them have a  reasonable nexus  with the object of preventing money laundering. The registration of an FIR is not a prerequisite for initiating proceedings under PMLA. The judgment in  Vijay Madanlal Choudhary does not mandate the registration of an FIR as a essential condition  for lodging a complaint or initiating action under PMLA.Moreover, The Delhi High Courtâs decision in  Vir Bhadra Singh v. Enforcement Directorate, and in P. Chidambaram v. Directorate of Enforcement,  the Supreme Court clarified that a  scheduled offence  is a sine qua non for money laundering, but registration of an FIR is not a prerequisite.To conclude the explanation I would say that your observations and legal analysis are precise and well-founded since the existence of a scheduled offence is the primary requirement and not an FIR, you may proceed with lodging a complaint with the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) if you have credible evidence or material suggesting the involvement of proceeds of crime. question: Can a FIR u/s 366 IPC be quashed where the accused is not at all involved where the accused was the 1st to report missing of the person and also has LIVE CCTV footage of her departing alone from the accused house leaving behind her grown up daughter of 17+. answer: Dear Client,To address a false FIR or false criminal proceedings if filed against any person, the aggrieved party can seek its quashing through a petition before the High Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973(now Sec.528 of BNSS). The Section 482 Cr. PC empowers the High Court to dismiss false FIR/criminal proceedings initiated under that FIR/complaint before the trial Court against a person. It is essential to prove before the court that the FIR/complaint or criminal suit was lodged with malicious intent to cause harm or inconvenience and is devoid of truth. The burden of proof rests on the petitioner. An application for the quashing of an FIR or criminal proceedings can also be filed before the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India through a Criminal Miscellaneous Writ Petition invoking the extraordinary jurisdiction of the Court to quash an FIR or criminal proceedings. The Chhattisgarh High Court has recently held that every abduction of a minor female cannot be regarded as an offence under Section 366 IPC [Kidnapping, abducting or inducing a woman to compel her marriage, etc these ingredients of such an offence must be corroborated by the victim's statement. The Hon'ble Allahabad High Court in the case of Smt. Malti Devi And Another Vs. - State Of U.P. And 3 Others, Citation No. - 2023:AHC:142613-DB held that the essential conditions for the application of Section 366 I.P.C. are that there is kidnapping or abduction of a woman with the intention to compel her or knowing it to be likely that she will be compelled to marry any person against her will or will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse and in the absence of the essential ingredients of Section 362 I.P.C. or even Section 366 I.P.C. a person cannot be held accused for the alleged offence. The Supreme Court also observed that an offence under Section 366 IPC would be attracted only when there is a forceful compulsion of marriage, by kidnapping or by inducing a woman. question: What action can I take against my mother in law if she has taken my gold without my permission.( Kochi, Kerala )
answer: Dear Client,As per Hindu law, Streedhan is whatever a woman receives during her lifetime including all movable, immovable property, gifts, etc received prior to marriage, at the time of marriage, and during childbirth. Even in situations where the divorce has not been dissolved by the judicial decree, as per the Supreme Court of India, the woman can always claim back her Streedhan from her in-laws. question: Can a primary petition be moved before hearing final appeal, highlighting grave errors in trial court judgment?( Kochi, Kerala )
answer: Dear Client,Yes, a primary petition can be filed before the appellate court to assert foul play in a trial court judgment even when a final appeal is pending. Rule 27 of the Order 41 of the CPC, 1908 permits the tendering of additional evidence or additional grounds for such reasons as may be necessary having reference to questions of law and fact involving substantial importance to the case which were not raised or, urged at the hearing of the former appeal. Where the errors are serious on the trail court the affected party could approach the appellate court through a Special Leave Petition SLP under Article 136 of the Constitution of India to draw the attention of the appellate court to them. To avoid making fatal mistakes it is wise to employ the service of a lawyer since the petition has to be written and backed up by reasons and evidence as provided under the law.Hope you find this answer suitable for resolving you query.

We are a Market Research company dealing with confidential data of our clients.
One of our employees, working with us for the past 7 years was asked to resign due to continuous non-performance in the past few months. His last working day was 31st March 2024.
He lied to everyone in our office that he is joining elsewhere. However, in the first week of May 2024, we came to know that he has started exact same business like our company.

answer: Dear Client,Every applicant applying for a passport or visa must go through a thorough process called immigration screening or immigration background checks. Visa/passport authorities often conduct background checks on the documents presented by an applicant to establish strong ties to their home country. A person accused of a criminal offence and whose case is pending for trial before the Court, may potentially affect and impact your USA visa. The specific impact will depend on the nature of the crime, the country to which the individual is applying for a visa, and the immigration laws of that country. You can get a visa/passport issued maybe for a short duration even during the pendency of criminal proceedings against you in court or before any law enforcement agency subject to permission of the concerned Court or law enforcement agency where the criminal proceeding is pending. The Allahabad High Court has ruled that a person's application for a visa/passport cannot be withheld merely on the ground that the applicant has a pending criminal case. Further, in the case of Poulami Basu vs The Government of India (2022 SCC OnLine Kar 1606), wherein a single Bench of Karnataka HC held that the right to travel abroad is a fundamental right guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

question: My mother has received death threat from my neighbor who is also our relative when my mother asked him to cut the mango tree which may fall on our house( North Goa, Goa )
answer: Dear Client,In the given scenario, your mother can lodge a complaint or FIR against the errant neighbor for blackmailing and criminal intimidation at the local police station under Sections 308 and 351(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita(BNS). Your mother can also file a petition praying for an Order of Protection in the City Civil Court or District Court. A Protective Order is a civil court order that is designed to stop violent and harassing behavior and to protect you from the abuser whose attitude or behavior appears to be life-threatening. There are two types of Protective Orders available for you. 1. Emergency Order of Protection (Ex Parte Emergency Order of Protection) - The Petition for Protective Order must clearly show that an act of abuse or threatening has occurred, 2. Regular Order of Protection (Non-emergency). There are no fees for filing a Protective Order. You do not need an Advocate to file for a Protective Order. However, if you wish, you can hire the service of an Advocate to represent you suitably before the Court to obtain a protective order. At the Show Cause hearing, you have to show and prove by adducing substantial evidence why you need the Protective Order. Apart from this, serving a legal notice to the errant neighbor your mother can file a private complaint against the neighbor in the court of the Magistrate under Section 223 of BNSS which outlines the procedure for a Magistrate to take cognizance of an offence. Upon receiving a complaint, the magistrate shall examine the complainant and any witnesses present. This examination is conducted under oath, and the substance of the examination is documented and signed by the complainant, witnesses, and the magistrate. If the magistrate finds sufficient grounds for proceeding with the case, he may issue a summons or warrant to the accused under Section 227 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023. If required, hire an Advocate to navigate the issue in the right way.

question:
My flat is G1 and adjacent flat is G2. My flat has been vacant from December 2024 to till date. every month i am getting around Rs-600-700 despite of zero consumption in my flat. recently i visited my flat along with electrician to check what is fault in my flat. Electrician found that there was no problem in the flat, issue is my energy meter has been tampered by adjacent (G2) flat. 
G2 owner has reverse both flat wiring connections. (he is the Electrician for our apartment). upon found i immediately reported issue to Local AE over the phone. and he sent the linemen to verify the same. line men came to out flat verified the issue and took the photographs. 
Upon linemen verification again I called to AE and asked what the further actions on that would be. He told me they would bookcase against G2 owner.  

Later working day, I called AE and enquired about the status of issue. He told me case was booked and notice would be sent to them. Then I requested acknowledgement of complaint he denied providing me.

After two days I visited AE office and submitted my return complaint in physical cop and took the acknowledgment. After todayâs again I visited AE office and requested case copy. Finally, they gave a copy to me.
Surprise point is here, that was I gave complaint on 19th April 2025 over the phone. But case was filed against G2 flat owner on 24-April-2025. And in the case file it was mentioned that accused power supply was terminated on 24-April-2025. Actual it was not disconnected till date. And they imposed fine of Rs-12000.
In the EB department their staff told me that G2 owner had sent register post to ADE stating that His meter was not working properly from last 6 months.
Considering these I understood that manipulations happened, and someone is trying to protect accused.

Then I sent a mail stating all the issues to CMD over past 7 days I havenât received any reply. Then I sent mail to Electrical Vigilance department. At last, I got response from Vigilance, they also visited apartment and investigated. After investigation one of the filed officers discussed with me over the phone and informed me. You must restore your connections with help of electrician and regarding financial loss I need to discuss with G2 Owner and settle it. They are not responsible for both the things. This was shocked to me. If they are not responsible on what basis case was filed and it was mentioned in the case file accused power supply was disconnected. 

How to deal with this and proceed further to get justice to my issue.( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 deals with electricity theft. This section specifically addresses activities such as meter tampering, illegal connections, and other forms of unauthorized use of electricity. When electricity theft is detected, an FIR must be registered, and the authorized officers under the Electricity Act have a responsibility to file this FIR within 24 hours of disconnection post detection of theft, which is an essential prerequisite before initiating any action against the offender for electricity theft. All the authorized/licensed Electricity Supply Agencies have their customer grievance redressal cell following the provision of sub-section 5 of Section 42 of the Electricity Act, 2003, which is handled by the designated Grievance Redressal Officer(GRO). You can escalate your grievance to the concerned GRO for a resolution to your grievance failing which you can approach the Electricity Ombudsman appointed by the State Electricity Regulatory Commission following the provisions of Sub-Section 6 of Section 42 of the Act who shall settle the grievance of an aggrieved consumer within such time as may be specified by the State Commission. Further, Project VIGEYE (Vigilance Eye) is a citizen-centric initiative, wherein citizens join hands with the Central Vigilance Commission in fighting corruption. Users can lodge their grievances and complaints online.

If any party attempts to pollute such a place by adopting recourse to make misrepresentation and is concealing material facts it does so at its risk and cost.Read a judgment about the above in Vijay Syal Vs. Intention is most important.False evidence is said to be given intentionally, if, the person making the statement is aware or has knowledge that it is false and has deliberately used such evidence in a judicial proceeding with the intention of deceiving the court .ELEMENTS OF PERJURY:1) False statement made by a person Who is âa) Bound by an oathb) By an express provision of lawc) A declaration which a person is bound by law to make on any subjectd) Which statement or declaration is false and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true.2. Now these petty criminals are harassing me by confronting me verbally and intimidate me.These criminals using a club as contact point to  peddle drugs. and harass passers by.  Kindly advise on legal course of action.( Kozhikode, Kerala )
answer: Dear Client,In the given scenario, lodge a complaint/FIR against the concerned petty criminals under Section 351 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita(BNS) for criminal intimidation. You can also file a private complaint against them in the court of the Magistrate under Section 223 of BNSS which outlines the procedure for a Magistrate to take cognizance of an offence. Upon receiving a complaint, the magistrate shall examine the complainant and any witnesses present. This examination is conducted under oath, and the substance of the examination is documented and signed by the complainant, witnesses, and the magistrate. If the magistrate finds sufficient grounds for proceeding with the case, he may issue a summons or warrant of arrest to the accused under Section 227 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023. You can also file a petition praying for an Order of Protection in the City Civil Court or District Court. A Protective Order is a civil court order that is designed to stop violent and harassing behavior and to protect you from the abuser whose attitude or behavior appears to be life-threatening. The Petition for Protective Order must clearly show that an act of abuse or threatening has occurred. There are no fees for filing a Protective Order. You do not need an Advocate to file for a Protective Order. However, if you wish, you can hire an Advocate to represent you suitably before the Court to obtain a protective order. At the Show Cause hearing, you have to show and prove by adducing substantial evidence why you need the Protective Order.
